original_question: Characterize completely the intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function satisfies μ(σ, τ) = 0.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1 poses the open problem of completely characterizing those intervals [σ, τ] in the classical permutation pattern poset whose Möbius function vanishes, stated after noting that many such zero-Möbius families are already known. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object (intervals [σ, τ] in the permutation pattern poset), the right invariant (the Möbius function), the right condition (μ(σ, τ) = 0), and the right level of ambition (a complete characterization). It is essentially the same open problem highlighted in §5.1. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper is working in the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment, i.e. σ ≤ τ means that σ occurs as a classical pattern in τ. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

To make the question stand alone, [σ, τ] should be defined as the interval {π ∈ P : σ ≤ π ≤ τ}; the paper also notes that if σ is not contained in τ then the interval is empty. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The Möbius function should be specified as the interval Möbius function of this poset, with μ(x, x) = 1 and μ(x, y) = -∑_{x≤z<y} μ(x, z) for x < y. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The quantifiers should be explicit: characterize all pairs of permutations σ, τ with σ ≤ τ. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The scope should remain the classical permutation pattern poset, not the consecutive-pattern poset or special subclasses such as separable permutations, even though those are discussed nearby as sources of partial results. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The nearby question about characterizing intervals for which |μ(σ, τ)| equals the number of occurrences of σ in τ is a different problem and should not be merged into the rewrite. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

This is not a numbered conjecture or theorem in the paper; it is an inline open problem in §5.1, so the refined version should preserve that narrow status rather than recast it as something broader. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: In the poset P of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment (so σ ≤ τ iff σ occurs as a classical pattern in τ), give a complete characterization of all pairs of permutations σ, τ with σ ≤ τ for which the interval [σ, τ] = {π ∈ P : σ ≤ π ≤ τ} has Möbius function value μ(σ, τ) = 0, where μ is defined recursively by μ(x, x) = 1 and μ(x, y) = -∑_{x≤z<y} μ(x, z) for x < y. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual intent: §5.1 explicitly singles out the problem of characterizing zero-Möbius intervals, after surveying partial results on Möbius values for special permutation classes. The only real sharpening needed is to make the ambient poset, the order relation, the interval notation, and the Möbius recursion explicit. The paper immediately separates this from a different neighboring problem about when |μ(σ, τ)| matches the number of occurrences of σ in τ, so that second question should not be folded into the refinement. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=907d621189adfb11324bde3f096bb79a478d180e&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
